reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 9.4(a) gives Ono a right 'but not the obligation' to Manufacture or use a Subcontractor, and 9.4(b) makes obtaining commercial requirements from Array an election, so there is no requirements-contract or sole-supplier obligation on us.

Array's undertaking in 9.1(a) to supply or secure supply of our requirements runs in our favour, and the Article II exclusive licence is exclusivity benefiting Customer, which the rule expressly treats as acceptable.

Section 8.2 'Exclusivity of Efforts' is a mutual, product-category-limited restriction on Commercializing Competing Products — the reciprocal of the exclusive licence — not a sourcing/sole-supplier covenant within this rule's detection guidance; noting it in the rationale rather than redlining it is consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed, and the deterministic check (no requirements/sole-supplier obligation remaining) passes.
